newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Q3 growth jumps, boosted by car buying.
newsitem.headline: French Q3 growth jumps, boosted by car buying.

text.p: France reported robust third-quarter economic growth on Thursday, powered by a rush to buy cars ahead of the end to a state subsidy scheme.

Gross domestic product (GDP) rose 0.9 percent after a revised decline of 0.2 percent in the second quarter, national statistics institute INSEE reported. It initially reported a 0.4 percent fall for the second quarter.
The rise was in line with expectations.
Economists said the big contributor to third-quarter growth came from consumers scrambling to take advantage of a state car buying subsidy which ended on September 30.
Growth was also spurred by a one percent rise in investment, with business increasing spending for the first time since the third quarter of 1995.
French finance minister Jean Arthuis said the third-quarter performance was in line with the government's forecast that the economy would expand by 1.3 percent in 1996.
"The government's forecast of 1.3 percent growth therefore appears plausible", Arthuis told reporters. "I confirm the 1996 forecast without ambiguity."
Economists said they expected a weak final quarter but that the worst of the economy's weakness may be over.
"The overall picture is that as in Germany, the economy has touched bottom," Christopher Potts, chief economist Cheuvreux de Virieu, told Reuters Financial Television.

"We will have a weak fourth quarter in terms of numbers. I think the number will be flat," he said. "It is not even impossible that we could have a negative GDP number in the fourth quarter, but it doesn't change the big picture."
